messages:
incidents-bot: Pager triggered: latency-slo-breach on gpu-pool-7 (p99 > 5s). Affected route: /v1/stream (chat streaming), metrics show sudden tail spike starting ~1770056700. Auto-escalation to oncall.
alex: I'm on it. Can someone post current p95/p99 and which node(s) are above threshold?
maya: backing up alex. I'll start pulling traces and check streaming stall traces.
lee: Observing large queue/backpressure in runtime. p95 ~900ms, p99 ~5400ms across pool. Only gpu-node-7-3 and gpu-node-7-5 show sustained GPU stalls.
jordan: Streaming stalls are correlated with long GPU stalls in the KV cache flush path. Getting logs now.
incidents-bot: Recent alerts: GPU ECC errors on gpu-node-7-5 (5 errors in last 10m), thermal_throttle events on gpu-node-7-3.
niko: Can we reduce concurrency to 1 on those nodes and drain traffic? I'll prep drain command.
alex: Do it. Also switch the traffic to dedicated-fallback-pool-2 for streaming routes and enable smaller model fallback for affected customers.
sam: I'll draft an initial customer impact note for CS to hold. Which customers hit highest error rates?
lee: Top impacted tenants: search-embeddings (20% requests delayed), comms-api (12% streaming stalls), analytics-batch minimal.
alex: jordan, can you run nvidia diagnostics on gpu-node-7-5 and paste output? Use sudo nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,THERMAL
jordan: paste follows:
```
# nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,THERMAL
GPU 0:
    ECC Errors (volatile):
        L1_CACHE: 3
        REGISTER_FILE: 1
    Thermal
        GpuCurrentTemp: 94 C
        Performance State: P2
        Applications Clocks: 1100 MHz
        Thermal Throttle: Active
```
jordan: ECC spikes + thermal throttle = likely hardware-level degradation. GPU 0 on 7-5 is flaking.
niko: Starting drain: kubectl drain node/gpu-node-7-5 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
ops-bot: Eviction started for node gpu-node-7-5. Pod disruption: 24 runtime pods.
maya: Routing change executed: all /v1/stream traffic routed off gpu-pool-7 to dedicated-fallback-pool-2 via routing-policy v2. Confirming no config drift.
alex: Also increased autoscale on dedicated-fallback-pool-2 by +30% to absorb burst.
lee: Applied model fallback: replace model `gptx-1-16k` -> `gptx-1-8k-quant` for streaming route for tenants flagged in fallback list.
sam: CS initial note: "We are investigating elevated latencies for streaming endpoints; mitigation in progress. We'll update in 30 minutes." Sending now to affected customers.
jordan: After drain started, p99 dropped from 5.4s -> 1.2s within 60s. p95 back to ~150ms.
niko: Node drain completed for gpu-node-7-5. Pods rescheduled. Node marked unschedulable. Marked for hardware investigation.
incidents-bot: New event: node gpu-node-7-3 reported thermal throttling and transient ECC correctable errors. Recommend similar drain if behavior repeats.
alex: We're seeing intermittent throttling on 7-3 as well. Start graceful cordon. jordan, can you run driver restart on 7-3 and monitor? If still flaking, drain.
jordan: Trying GPU driver restart:
```
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced
sudo modprobe -r nvidia_uvm && sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm
# tail -n 50 /var/log/nvidia-installer.log
```
jordan: Driver restart completed. Temps dropped from 92C -> 68C. No new ECC increments in the last 2m.
lee: Runtime latency stabilized. p99 ~650ms now. Streaming stalls resolved for most flows.
alex: Good. We'll keep 7-3 cordoned for 30m and run extended burn tests. 7-5 is already flagged for RMA.
niko: Opening hardware ticket to vendor with ECC dump attached and serial numbers. Ticket ID: HW-2026-0893. Requesting expedited RMA.
sam: Notifying top 3 affected customers with status update: mitigation applied, traffic rerouted, ongoing monitoring. CS will provide ETA once RMA scheduled.
maya: I'm collecting traces for postmortem and will seed a short eval to detect regressions caused by fallback models.
alex: Summary of actions taken:
- Detected p99 breach on /v1/stream triggered pager
- Identified GPU hardware degradation (ECC + thermal) on gpu-node-7-5; thermal events on 7-3
- Drained and cordoned 7-5; driver restart and cordon on 7-3
- Rerouted traffic to dedicated-fallback-pool-2 and enabled model fallback
- CS notified affected customers; status page updated
- Opened hardware RMA ticket

jordan: Current metrics snapshot (after mitigation): p95:120ms, p99:650ms, error-rate streaming: 0.6% (down from 4.8%).
incidents-bot: Incident severity update: from P2 -> P3 (customer impact reduced, mitigation in place). Please file postmortem within 72h.
alex: I'll own the postmortem. maya, collect traces and timeline. niko, confirm RMA schedule and follow up with hardware team.
maya: Will do. I'll also add a follow-up task to add GPU thermal SLO alerting to catch rising temps before thermal throttle.
niko: RMA scheduled for 2026-03-19 09:00 PT. Replacement GPU to be installed during low traffic window.
sam: CS will send final customer update after postmortem published.
alex: Great work team. Any remaining action items before we close this thread?
lee: I'll run a quick canary workload against gpu-pool-7 to validate no regressions once 7-3 is uncordoned.
jordan: I'll attach the ECC log and driver restart steps to the hardware ticket.
maya: I'll draft the incident timeline and link to traces in the postmortem doc.
alex: Closing note: If any new thermal or ECC alerts surface, re-open and page immediately. Thanks :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Incident marked resolved in PagerDuty. Reminder: submit postmortem within 72h at /incidents/postmortems/new
